title: The difficulty: living faith and some love of God precede justification
source_text: XXVII. Hac autem in parte videtur doctrina Protestantium non carere difficultate. Et enim qui inter eos de rebus Theologicis accuratius Philosophantur, agnoscunt fidem, eamque vivam & actuosam, esse conditionem ad justificationem hominis praerequisitam. Jam vero credere in Deum est quoddam opus vere bonum, neque fides viva est sine aliqua Dei dilectione, quae ipsa quoque est quoddam bonum opus; adeoque opera quaedam quae justificationem praecedunt, sunt vere bona.
pass_a_gloss: XXVII. But in this part the doctrine of the Protestants seems not to lack difficulty. For those who among them on Theological matters more accurately Philosophize, acknowledge faith, and that living and active, to be a condition to the justification of man prerequisite. But now to believe in God is a certain work truly good, nor is living faith without some love of God, which itself also is a certain good work; and so certain works which precede justification, are truly good.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXVII. On this point, however, Protestant doctrine does not seem free from difficulty. Those among them who reason most exactly about theological matters acknowledge that faith, and a living and active faith, is a prerequisite condition of a man's justification.
Yet believing in God is a truly good work, and living faith does not exist without some love of God, which is itself a good work too. So some works that precede justification are truly good.
